Equity Research
European Luxury Goods & Specialty Retail
30 July 2026
Hermes
Beyond the Print: Debate on algo remains unresolved

Q2 cFx sales grew +6.7% cFX (vs. +6.5% cons.), with LG +10.2% cFX (vs. +10.7% cons.). H1 EBIT margin of 41% was a beat, driving a c.1% upgrade to our EPS estimates. Beyond the print, <8% cFx cannot fully dispel investor concerns around the sustainability of Group and LG growth algorithm. Remain EW.
Results key take: In line. Hermes reported Q2-26 revenue of €4.1bn and cFX growth of 6.7%, which was overall in line with cons. of 6.5%. Leather Goods drove growth at 10.2% cFX, below cons. at 10.7%.

Results details: By region: Growth in 2Q26 was driven by the Americas at 13.7% and Japan at 12.3%, confirming trends seen across peers. APAC excl. Japan remained the weaker spot, up 2.5% and below consensus of 3.2%. Europe and France were solid, with France up 6.2% cFX, beating consensus of 3.8%, and Europe excl. France up 8.3% cFX. By metier: Leather Goods drove growth once again, up 10.2% cFX, but below cons. of 10.7% and the 11-12% algorithm. The RTW & Accessories division grew 3.6% cFX, in line with cons. at 3.5%, continuing to be a drag on the group's performance. The Silk & Textiles division grew 12.2% cFX, a strong beat vs cons. of 7.5% in a category that is typically more exposed to the aspirational consumer. The Perfumes & Beauty division reported a negative -9.5% cFX growth, well below cons. of -1.5%.

Revisions: FY26 cFx growth of 7%, EPS up c1%: We lower our top-line estimates for 3Q26 from 8.6% to 7.6%, as we take a more cautious view on APAC given continued weakness. We only slightly lower our Leather Goods 3Q26 growth by 50bps to 11.0%, and cut RTW growth by the same amount. We take larger cuts in Perfumes and Cosmetics. This brings us to a FY26 growth forecast of 7.0% cFX at group level, from 7.3% previously. We increase our FY26 EBIT margin estimate to 40.8% following the beat in H1. Our estimate changes imply a c.1% EPS increase in FY26-28 (Figure 11). We keep our PT unchanged at EUR 1,700 with unchanged DCF assumptions at 7.5% WACC and 3.5% long-term growth.

Beyond results, key debate remains unresolved despite lower valuations. Hermès remains one of the most debated luxury stocks (see our feedback note from 100+ meetings with investors). 2Q results have not provided confidence in the sustainability of the growth model. Importantly, capacity expansion plans remain consistent with 6–7% volume growth (Figure 8), supporting our view that supply should not be a constraint through 2030 and raising concerns

Why EQUAL WEIGHT?

Thanks to its high level of exclusivity, superior growth and resilient margins, Hermes is one of the highest-quality stocks that we have under coverage. However, a slow start to 2026 and disruption from MENA may raise investor concerns around growth levels going forward.
Hermes maintains strong double-digit sales growth and EBIT margin reaches the mid 40s range.

Assume single-digit top-line growth as other segments grow at mid-single digits, diluting the higher structural growth of the Leather Goods division. EBIT margin remains in the 36-37% range. Terminal growth set at 2.5%.

Beyond the print: the growth algorithm debate is still on
"There is no way Hermes will be trading anywhere close to its current multiple in 12 months. It will either be much higher or much lower"
— Investor, early June 2026

Key debate still on and the valuations are down. Hermès is one of the most debated names in our coverage universe. Unfortunately, 2Q results did not provide the confidence needed for the bull case and bullet-proof sustainability of the business model, leaving room for the bear debate to continue.

Bull and Bear views: Bulls view current valuation levels as an extremely attractive entry point and see the recent slowdown as temporary. Bears, by contrast, argue that the desirability of iconic bags has weakened, competition for the high-end consumer has intensified, and softer trends in ex-leather métiers signal lower barriers to quota bag purchases pointing to an extended slowdown and potential change in leather goods growth algorithm, which implies 6% volume growth.

What does the company say: The company continues to highlight challenges in APAC and no major sequential change/acceleration in all regions except for MENA and France, both impacted by tourism and MENA consumer. While Leather Goods growth remains strong at +DD (10.2% in 2Q26), this is below the FY growth algorithm of 11-12% growth with c.6% volume contribution, but we believe 6% volume expectation is still in place (despite somewhat less clear communication at the conference call).

What does the company do? Expand capacity for 6-7% volume growth: Our analysis suggests supply is there, at least until 2030, with the number of production employees, the closest proxy, growing at c.7% 5Y CAGR in 25-30E (our estimates), 1% below the previous decade.

We employ production employees as a proxy to understand volume constraints and the investments needed to sustain c.6% volume growth going forward. We estimate that Hermes' capacity expansion should allow 6-7% volume growth in the next 5 years, in line with our Leather Goods forecasts. As a result, we expect the metier to expand to c.49% of Hermes' sales by 2030 from c.44% in 2025.

...In this context, change in algorithm could be painful: We believe that the Leather Goods demand model remains intact and we assume that there are no material risks to our mid-to-long-term volume assumptions. Any major changes in demand in leather goods could raise concerns around over-investment and over-capacity, and could put significant pressure on margins and returns.

What is the (soft) data saying: Outside of anecdotal evidence, we have not been able to find data to indicate 1) lower demand for iconic bags, 2) materially increased supply of iconic bags in resale (we have some comments on increase in availability of "other" bags, though), 3) deterioration of price premium for iconic bags in resale (on the opposite) and 4) lower required spend needed to qualify for quota bag purchase at Hermes store. Our interviews with industry participants, including a brick and mortar Hermes reseller, suggest increase, not decrease, of resale premium, given recent price increases.

What we think: For FY26, we are more comfortable with 10.5% FY growth in metier, with 11/12% in 3/4Q26 rather than FY. We believe Leather Goods could comfortably deliver HSD-LDD (we are at 10.5%) CAGR in 26-29. Our EW rating is focused on 1) 2026 market challenges, which underpin our below-consensus estimates of c.8% cFX growth over FY27–29e; 2) medium-term risks in Asia Pacific (52% of sales incl. Japan), where we forecast c.7% CAGR; 3) confidence in longer-term scalability of the artisanal model.

Valuation is becoming more compelling, but we think the stock needs clear evidence that group growth can sustainably re-accelerate into the HSD range, whether via Leather Goods or stronger non-Leather métiers momentum. We do not expect 3Q26 to be that catalyst (cFX growth 7.6%).

Model Update

We lower our top-line growth estimates for 3Q26 from 8.3% to 7.6%, as we take a more cautious view on APAC given continued weakness. We only slightly lower our Leather Goods 3Q26 growth by 50bps to 11.0%, and cut RTW growth by the same amount. We take larger cuts in Perfumes and Cosmetics. This brings us to a FY26 growth forecast of 7.0% cFX at group level, from 7.3% previously.

As far as the gross margin is concerned, we leave our 2H26 GM forecast unchanged at 71.3%, down 30bp y/y. Overall, we increase our FY26 EBIT margin estimate to 40.8% following the beat in H1. Our estimate changes imply a c.1% EPS increase in FY26-28. We keep our PT unchanged at EUR 1,700 with unchanged DCF assumptions at 7.5% WACC and 3.5% long-term growth. We remain EW.

Guide to the BARC Fundamental Equity Research Rating System:

Our coverage analysts use a relative rating system in which they rate stocks as Overweight, Equal Weight or Underweight (see definitions below) relative to other companies covered by the analyst or a team of analysts that are deemed to be in the same industry (the "industry coverage universe").

In addition to the stock rating, we provide industry views which rate the outlook for the industry coverage universe as Positive, Neutral or Negative (see definitions below). A rating system using terms such as buy, hold and sell is not the equivalent of our rating system. Investors should carefully read the entire research report including the definitions of all ratings and not infer its contents from ratings alone.
Stock Rating
Overweight - The stock is expected to outperform the unweighted expected total return of the industry coverage universe over a 12-month investment horizon.
Equal Weight - The stock is expected to perform in line with the unweighted expected total return of the industry coverage universe over a 12-month investment horizon.
Underweight - The stock is expected to underperform the unweighted expected total return of the industry coverage universe over a 12-month investment horizon.

Rating Suspended - The rating and target price have been suspended temporarily due to market events that made coverage impracticable or to comply with applicable regulations and/or firm policies in certain circumstances including where the Investment Bank of BARC Bank PLC is acting in an advisory capacity in a merger or strategic transaction involving the company.
Industry View
Positive - industry coverage universe fundamentals/valuations are improving.
Neutral - industry coverage universe fundamentals/valuations are steady, neither improving nor deteriorating.
Negative - industry coverage universe fundamentals/valuations are deteriorating.

Valuation Methodology: Our price target is based on a DCF where we assume an equity risk premium of 4.2% and a beta of 1.1, leading to a WACC of 7.5%. Considering Hermes' top-line growth outperformance and higher resilience, we assume long-term growth of 3.5% vs 2.5% for the sector.

Risks which May Impede the Achievement of the BARC Valuation and Price Target: Risks to the downside include slowdown in demand, particularly in Asia and sustainability of growth algorithm in leather goods at scale. Beyond that, a much weaker macro environment than expected could have a stronger impact on the high-end consumer cohort, which is usually perceived as more resilient. Upside risks include significant acceleration of APAC/China demand, immediate recovery of MENA cohort to DD growth, significant expansion outside Leather Goods division.
